memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'"When a leader sins unintentionally and does what is forbidden in any of the commands of the LORD his God, when he realises his guilt and the sin he has committed becomes known, he must bring as his offering a male goat without defect."'" - Lev 4:22-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Now the tribal leader — the civil ruler, the man with authority over people's daily lives. And notice the difference in his offering. Not a bull, but a male goat.

His sin was serious, but its reach was narrower than the high priest's, whose failure touched the nation's relationship with God itself. God calibrates precisely. He is neither careless nor excessive.

But look closely at one phrase: the commands of the LORD his God. That expression is not used of the priest or the community. It is added here, for the ruler.

It is a quiet reminder to a man with power that he is still under authority. He gives orders all day. He judges disputes. People obey him. And God says: remember whose you are. The LORD is still his God.

Power has a way of eroding accountability. The more we decide for others, the easier it becomes to stop submitting ourselves. Every ruler in Israel who forgot this ended badly.

Jesus, who had all authority, said He came not to be served but to serve (Mk 10:45). Paul reminded Christians that there is no authority except that which God has established (Rom 13:1).

Whatever authority you hold — over employees, children, students, a congregation — you hold it under Someone.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where do I have authority, and am I exercising it as someone under God's authority?
2. Has any area of my life quietly stopped being accountable to anyone?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, whatever influence You have given me, keep me mindful that You remain my God. Guard me from using authority as though I answered to no one. Amen.
